solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tie up, seeing low resistance

parts.note: to low is to moo, the noise a cow makes
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone notices weak opposition while knotting something.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to tie it up at a quay or buoy.

clue.text: Loadsamoney for throwing game — and resists

indicators.note: throwing the word game about scatters its letters into a new order

parts.note: to buck is to resist or oppose, as in bucking a trend

explanation.surface: Someone earns a fortune by losing a match on purpose while defying authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' rearranges GAME into MEGA. Loadsamoney is British slang for a huge amount of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang terms for a vast sum of cash.

clue.text: Engineers need more recent track studies

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
fresher means newer, more recent
a course is a track, as for racing

explanation.surface: Army engineers require the latest railway research.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a programme of study updating earlier training.

clue.text: Supporting worker in arrears

parts.note: to be behind someone is to support them
a hand is a manual worker, as a farm hand

explanation.surface: A helpful employee has fallen behind with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand is an old word for late or overdue, especially with payments.

clue.text: Be protective of broken heart, and show a sign of life

indicators.note: being protective of something means wrapping round it, so these letters go outside
a broken heart is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A caring friend guards a heartbroken person, who barely shows signs of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like the start of an instruction, but it is the container's letters; 'protective of' and 'broken' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing is the basic evidence that someone is still alive.

clue.text: Presenter gets mature person captive to fortune

parts.note: a host presents a television show
to age is to mature, grow older

explanation.surface: A TV host acquires an older companion at the mercy of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'a hostage to fortune', something that leaves you exposed to future misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held as security is at the mercy of events, hence the idiom of fortune's captive.

clue.text: Regain control across the heart of dairy country

indicators.note: one piece lies across another, spanning it on both sides
to bring the letters of regain under control is to put them in a new order
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A farmer wins back command of a dairy region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'control' rearranges REGAIN into NIGERA, and 'across' spreads it around I, the middle letter of 'dairy' picked by 'the heart of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a large nation in West Africa.

clue.text: In bed, they're always full of trouble!

definitions.text: In bed, they're always full of trouble!

parts.words: In bed, they're always full of trouble!
parts.note: being in hot water means being in trouble; these bedtime warmers are literally full of hot water

explanation.surface: Troublemakers who are always found under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber bags filled with heated water are placed in beds to warm them.

clue.text: Head of entertainment invested in clothes and fancy dressers

indicators.note: invested here means clothed in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: duds is slang for clothes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An entertainment boss wears smart outfits for a costume party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' gives E, and 'invested in' places it inside DUDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudes, originally, were dandies who dressed showily.

clue.text: Labourers needed to put beams on top of garage

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting something on another places it after it
the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rafters are the sloping beams of a roof

explanation.surface: Builders are required to fit roof timbers on a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' picks G from 'garage'; 'on' sets RAFTERS after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grafters are hard workers, British slang for those who toil.

clue.text: Upset at being drawn

definitions.meaning: a drawn fish or bird has had its innards removed

explanation.definitionFit: Gutted means both devastated and disembowelled, as when a cook draws a chicken.

clue.text: Divide group chasing sound purchase

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes second
sound tells us the word is heard rather than read, giving its pronunciation

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A faction pursues a good bargain, then splits.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable ('a sound purchase'), but it signals a homophone; 'chasing' means following.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts.

clue.text: Affected manners include greeting frequencies

indicators.note: one piece includes another by holding it inside

parts.note: putting on airs means behaving affectedly
a wave is a gesture of greeting

explanation.surface: Pretentious people greet each other at radio stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected manners' means pretentious behaviour, as in putting on airs; 'include' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The airwaves are the radio frequencies used for broadcasting.

clue.text: Close friends have it

indicators.note: the word friends has these letters within it

explanation.surface: Intimate companions possess it.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of something is its finish.

clue.text: Material that's just on the money

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another follows it

parts.note: cash is money
mere means just, only

explanation.surface: A fabric is priced exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just on the money' reads as 'exactly right', but 'just' is a synonym and 'on' places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine wool fabric from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: When PM starts and makes changes

parts.note: the afternoon begins as the morning, AM, ends
the afternoon begins as the morning, AM, ends

explanation.surface: A new Prime Minister takes office and revises policy.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is read as post meridiem, the afternoon, not the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter, so amends means alters.

clue.text: Little heraldic symbols on weapons

parts.note: small means little
arms are the devices on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: Tiny crests decorate guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are firearms carried by hand.

clue.text: Rush into outwardly serious investments

indicators.note: one piece goes into another
the outward letters of a word are its first and last

parts.note: to hare is to rush about

explanation.surface: A trader dashes headlong into grave dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives S and S from 'serious'; 'into' puts HARE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are units of stock bought as investments.

clue.text: Chaucer regularly demonstrated such colour

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A medieval poet showed off a particular shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a shade or tint.

clue.text: Status diminished by reserve

indicators.note: diminished means made smaller, so a letter is taken off

parts.note: standing means status

explanation.surface: Someone's prestige is reduced by a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute, as a reserve is.

clue.text: Shape of curve described by Moor in almost Arctic environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so these letters go round it
almost means one letter short

parts.note: the Arctic is polar
the Moors were Muslims of North Africa, hence an Arab

explanation.surface: A North African traces an arc in the icy north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims POLAR to POLA, which as the 'environment' surrounds ARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is a particular U-shaped curve.

clue.text: Almost immaculate outfit for a hobby

indicators.note: almost means one letter short of the full word

parts.note: pure means immaculate
a suit is an outfit

explanation.surface: A nearly spotless costume for a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final E of PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an activity followed for pleasure.

clue.text: Arrives and delivers a sermon topless!

indicators.note: topless means without the top letter, in a down clue the first

parts.note: to preach is to deliver a sermon

explanation.surface: A vicar turns up and preaches without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive there.

clue.text: Elegant posh young lady broadcasting?

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, an upper-class girl entering society
on air means broadcasting

explanation.surface: A stylish debutante appears on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and stylishly charming.

clue.text: Greek party trick uncovered

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: uncovered means losing the outer letters

explanation.surface: A trick from Greece is exposed at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' takes the first and last letters off 'trick', leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is a Greek dialect and an order of Greek architecture.

clue.text: Annual arts awards having backing of the stars

indicators.note: backing means read backwards
the clue words have these letters within them

explanation.surface: Yearly arts prizes have the support of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' holds LARTSA within 'Annual arts awards'; 'backing' turns it round. 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but means heavenly bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to the stars.

clue.text: Inflexible person making charge stick

parts.note: to ram is to charge into
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A rigid person turns a bayonet charge into a poke.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is used figuratively for a stiff, unbending person.

clue.text: Champion — the one who has the trophy having lost lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means dropping the first letter

parts.words: the one who has the trophy
parts.note: a cup holder holds the trophy

explanation.surface: The title-holder has lost the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholder is a supporter, and to champion is to support.

clue.text: Fiddle cost, or even get some insurance papers

indicators.note: to fiddle the words is to rearrange them, punning on fiddling accounts

explanation.surface: A fraudster fiddles the costs or gets even with insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: A cover note is a British temporary insurance certificate issued before the policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover notes are interim documents proving insurance cover.

clue.text: Reserves making advances

definitions.meaning: a sub is a loan paid ahead of wages

explanation.definitionFit: Subs are both substitute players and wage advances.
